q: On 28 May the CFO says the board meeting has moved to 30 May and asks the team to sign on 29 May, with three confirmations and the inventory rollforward still incomplete. BEST response?
o: Sign on 29 May and finish the open confirmations within the assembly window
Sign with an emphasis of matter paragraph on the incomplete confirmations
Explain the report date cannot precede the evidence and propose a new date
Issue a qualified opinion for scope limitation to meet the board deadline
why: The report date must not be earlier than the date sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained, and the assembly window covers administrative assembly only, not fresh evidence gathering. Qualifying is premature while alternative procedures remain possible.

q: Management refuses to let you send a balance confirmation to a large debtor, saying the relationship is delicate. The balance is Rs 4 crore out of Rs 22 crore receivables. What should the auditor do FIRST?
o: Accept the refusal and move to testing subsequent receipts and dispatch notes
Inquire into the reasons for the refusal and weigh the fraud risk implications
Treat it as a scope limitation and qualify the opinion on receivables now
Ask the client to obtain the signed confirmation and pass it to the team
why: SA 505 requires the auditor to inquire into the reasons for a management refusal and evaluate the implications for fraud risk before deciding on alternative procedures. Client obtained confirmations lack the required auditor control over the process.

q: Vouching consultancy expenses reveals Rs 90 lakh paid to a firm where a director spouse is a partner. It is absent from the related party note and management calls it immaterial and at arm length. BEST response?
o: Accept the arm length representation and record the discussion in the file
Report the payment directly to the Registrar of Companies as an offence
Report it as a key audit matter and proceed with the remaining audit work
Test it against the related party definition and inform the audit committee
why: Related party disclosure is triggered by the relationship rather than by the size of the amount, so completeness of the related party listing must be tested and the matter communicated to those charged with governance. A representation on arm length pricing is not sufficient appropriate evidence.

q: Analytics show 34 manual journals posted by the finance controller after cut-off, all round-sum credits to revenue reversed next period. Management calls them provisioning corrections. BEST response?
o: Extend journal testing, examine the support and revise the fraud risk
Obtain a written representation from the controller explaining the entries
Report the controller to the audit committee before any further testing
Review only entries above performance materiality to protect the budget
why: Round-sum post cut-off entries reversed in the next period are a classic management override indicator, and SA 240 requires extended journal testing and reassessment of fraud risk. A written representation is not audit evidence and escalation before any factual basis is premature.

q: Two days before signing you learn the client largest customer, giving 46 percent of revenue, has terminated its contract and the working capital loan matures in four months with no sanction for renewal. BEST course?
o: Disclose it in the notes as a subsequent event and sign an unmodified opinion
Withdraw from the engagement because the going concern basis is now doubtful
Obtain a twelve month cash flow assessment and evaluate the management plans
Issue an adverse opinion because the going concern basis has clearly failed
why: SA 570 requires evaluation of managements assessment covering at least twelve months from the balance sheet date, with an unmodified opinion plus a material uncertainty section where disclosure is adequate. An adverse opinion applies only if the going concern basis itself is inappropriate.

q: Accumulated uncorrected misstatements total Rs 46 lakh against overall materiality of Rs 50 lakh. All are judgemental provision estimates that reduce expense. BEST audit response?
o: Conclude they are immaterial because the total sits below overall materiality
Weigh the one directional bias, seek correction and report the items to TCWG
Reduce materiality to Rs 40 lakh so that a qualification becomes necessary
Net them against unrecorded items in the other direction to reduce the total
why: SA 450 requires evaluation of qualitative aspects, and consistent one directional bias in estimates can indicate a lack of neutrality even when the arithmetic total falls below materiality. Retrospectively adjusting materiality to engineer an outcome is not acceptable.

q: Eleven days after the audit report date but before issuance, the auditor learns a fire destroyed inventory of Rs 7 crore that existed at year end, the fire having occurred after year end. BEST response?
o: Do nothing, since no procedures are required after the audit report date
Recall and reissue the report under the original date with disclosure added
Raise the matter at the annual general meeting without telling management
Discuss with management and issue a new or dual dated report once amended
why: SA 560 requires discussion with management for facts becoming known after the report date, and a new or amended report if the financial statements are amended. Keeping the original date would falsely imply the evidence covered the later event.

q: You believe a Rs 1.2 crore capitalised development cost fails the recognition criteria. Your engagement manager disagrees and instructs you to clear the workpaper. What should you do?
o: Document your view and escalate under the difference of opinion process
Clear the workpaper, since the manager is senior and owns the conclusion
Send the manager an email recording your disagreement and then sign off
Take the matter directly to the client audit committee for a final ruling
why: SQC 1 and SA 220 require a documented process for resolving differences of professional opinion, with the matter concluded before the report is released. An informal email does not discharge that requirement and going to the client bypasses the firm improperly.

q: A long standing client whose fee is 18 percent of total firm revenue hints the audit will be re-tendered if this year is difficult. BEST safeguard focused response?
o: Reduce scope in low risk areas so the fee stays within the agreed budget
Treat the fee pressure as commercial reality, since no rule is breached
Evaluate the self interest threat and apply an engagement quality review
Resign at once, because fee dependence always impairs auditor independence
why: Undue fee dependence creates self interest and intimidation threats that must be evaluated and addressed through safeguards such as an independent quality review or consultation. Cutting scope to protect a fee is a direct impairment and resignation is a last resort.

q: A junior client accounts assistant has raised vendor invoices to a shell firm totalling Rs 11 lakh. The CFO says he will handle it privately and asks the auditor not to escalate. BEST action?
o: Accept the CFO assurance, since the amount is well below overall materiality
Communicate it to those charged with governance and test for wider failure
Report the matter to the police directly, since fraud is a criminal offence
Add an emphasis of matter paragraph on the fraud and do no further work
why: SA 240 requires timely communication of employee fraud to those charged with governance irrespective of amount, and consideration of whether it signals broader control failure. Agreeing to suppress the matter compromises the auditor responsibility.

q: Company X has turnover of Rs 300 crore. The team identifies suspected fraud by senior management of Rs 1.4 crore. Under the Companies Act 2013, what is the correct reporting route?
o: Report only to the audit committee, since the amount is below Rs 5 crore
Mention it in the auditor report, as Government reporting covers listed firms
Report the matter to the ICAI disciplinary directorate for further action
Report to the Central Government after the board intimation and reply process
why: Section 143(12) read with Rule 13 requires reporting suspected fraud of Rs 1 crore or more to the Central Government after seeking the board or audit committee reply, with smaller amounts reported to the board or audit committee. The threshold is amount based, not listing based.

q: During physical verification you observe the store keeper counting only the aisles the auditor pointed to, using count sheets pre-printed with book quantities. BEST immediate response?
o: Perform independent two way test counts and assess the count reliability
Accept the count, since physical verification is a management responsibility
Qualify the opinion on inventory at once for unreliable count procedures
Rely on the perpetual records, since they agree with all the count sheets
why: Pre-printed book quantities create anchoring bias and directed counting undermines the exercise, so independent counts from floor to sheet and sheet to floor are needed. Agreement of sheets to perpetual records proves nothing when the sheets were populated from those records.

q: The group CFO offers your team a fully paid weekend at a resort to thank them after a difficult audit. Your manager calls it customary hospitality. BEST response?
o: Accept now, since the report is signed and independence no longer applies
Accept but disclose the trip in the annual firm independence declaration
Decline, since hospitality above trivial value creates unmanaged threats
Accept only the amount the firm would have spent on team travel anyway
why: Gifts and hospitality of other than trivial and inconsequential value create threats that no safeguard can eliminate, so refusal is the only correct response. Signing the report does not end the obligation because the relationship continues into the next period.

q: The client changed the useful life of plant from 15 to 22 years in the final quarter, lifting profit by Rs 3.6 crore and just meeting a debt covenant. BEST response?
o: Accept it as a change in accounting estimate applied wholly prospectively
Evaluate the technical basis and whether the covenant timing shows bias
Treat it as a prior period error and restate all comparative figures
Report it as a key audit matter without any further audit procedures
why: A change in estimate is valid only where supported by objective evidence, and late timing combined with a covenant benefit is a strong indicator of management bias requiring evaluation under SA 540. Accepting it automatically skips that required evaluation.

q: A prospective client asks your firm to be statutory auditor while an affiliate of the firm already maintains its accounting records and prepares its financial statements. BEST response?
o: Accept, provided entirely different personnel perform the two services
Accept but disclose the bookkeeping arrangement clearly in the report
Accept if the client audit committee formally approves the arrangement
Decline, since keeping the books of an audit client is a barred service
why: Maintaining the books of account of an audit client creates a self review threat that no safeguard cures, and Section 144 of the Companies Act also prohibits it for companies. Separate personnel or audit committee approval cannot override a prohibition.

q: You are the audit senior. Two days before the deadline you realise a sampling error meant only 12 of the required 40 revenue items were tested, and results are already summarised. BEST action?
o: Extend the sample now, tell the manager and re-evaluate before sign off
Record a revised judgement on sample size and conclude on the items tested
Complete the remaining 28 items after signing during the assembly period
Project the error rate from the 12 items over the population and conclude
why: The conclusion cannot be supported unless the planned sample is completed, and immediate escalation lets the team correct it before the report date. Documenting a post hoc change in judgement to cover the error misrepresents the workpaper.

q: Management gives you a legal confirmation but instructs the lawyer not to comment on a pending tax matter of Rs 9 crore that you learnt of from board minutes. BEST response?
o: Rely on the board minutes and record the contingency amount as disclosed
Lower the assessed litigation risk, since the matter is now already known
Treat it as an imposed scope limitation and inform the audit committee
Obtain a management representation covering all litigation and conclude
why: Preventing the auditor from communicating with legal counsel on a known matter is an imposed limitation on scope requiring TCWG communication and possible modification of the opinion. Board minutes do not provide the legal assessment of outcome and quantum.

q: In a first year audit the opening inventory of Rs 18 crore was audited by the predecessor, whose file is unavailable, and the client bars any opening balance procedures. Effect on the report?
o: No effect, since opening balances remain with the predecessor auditor
Possible qualification or disclaimer on the profit and loss statement
An adverse opinion on the financial statements considered as a whole
An unmodified opinion with an other matter paragraph on the predecessor
why: SA 510 makes the incoming auditor responsible for evidence that opening balances do not materially misstate the current period, and inability to verify opening inventory affects the reported result. Naming a predecessor does not discharge that responsibility.
